podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Career Impact and Fans
podcast.body: While neither X-Ray Spex nor her solo career produced numerous hits, Paulie Styrin earned considerable respect from influential figures in music, including U2, who were major fans of her work. "And while neither X-Ray Specks or her solo career produced a lot of hits, Paulie earned a lot of respect from some big names. You too was on record as being a major fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Challenging Female Image
podcast.body: Paulie Styrin intentionally subverted the typical image of a female singer. As a mixed-race individual (Irish mother, Somali father), she was comfortable with her body type and weight, wore wild, day-glo clothing, and had prominent braces on her teeth, making her a highly unconventional and inspiring figure. "Part of her thing was to disabuse everyone of what the typical female singer should look like."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Identity and Punk Entry
podcast.body: Born Marion Joan Elliott Saeed in South London, she adopted the stage name Paulie Styrin, which she described as a "fake plastic name." Her entry into the 1970s punk scene was prompted by seeing the Sex Pistols perform in the summer of 1976, after which she formed X-Ray Spex following an attempt at a solo career. "Her real name was Marion Joan Elliott Saeed. She was from South London and also got second to the 1970s punk scene after seeing the Sex Pistols in the summer of 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Later Life and Death
podcast.body: Paulie Styrin faced significant personal challenges, including a diagnosis of bipolar disorder in 1991, followed by a breast cancer diagnosis. She ultimately passed away from breast cancer in 2011 at the age of 53. "She was diagnosed as bipolar in 1991 and then found out she had breast cancer. That killed her at the age of 53 in 2011."
